scores.name: Rodwell haematological scoring system (HSS) for neonatal sepsis
scores.purpose: Early diagnosis of neonatal sepsis from the blood count and peripheral smear.
scores.quote: Minimum score that can be obtained is 0 and maximum score, 8.

options.label: Abnormal
options.quote: HSS assigns a score of 1 for each of seven findings significantly associated with sepsis: Abnormal total leukocyte count, abnormal total PMN count, elevated immature PMN count, elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio, immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio ≥0.3, platelet count ≤150,000/mm 3 , and pronounced degenerative or toxic changes in PMNs.

options.label: Abnormal
options.quote: HSS assigns a score of 1 for each of seven findings significantly associated with sepsis: Abnormal total leukocyte count, abnormal total PMN count, elevated immature PMN count, elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio, immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio ≥0.3, platelet count ≤150,000/mm 3 , and pronounced degenerative or toxic changes in PMNs.

options.label: Abnormal, with no mature PMNs seen on smear
options.quote: An abnormal total PMN count is assigned score of two instead of 1, if no mature polymorphs are seen on the peripheral smear to compensate for the low I:M ratio

options.label: Elevated
options.quote: HSS assigns a score of 1 for each of seven findings significantly associated with sepsis: Abnormal total leukocyte count, abnormal total PMN count, elevated immature PMN count, elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio, immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio ≥0.3, platelet count ≤150,000/mm 3 , and pronounced degenerative or toxic changes in PMNs.

items.label: Elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio

options.quote: HSS assigns a score of 1 for each of seven findings significantly associated with sepsis: Abnormal total leukocyte count, abnormal total PMN count, elevated immature PMN count, elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio, immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio ≥0.3, platelet count ≤150,000/mm 3 , and pronounced degenerative or toxic changes in PMNs.

items.label: Immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio 0.3 or more

options.label: 0.3 or more

options.label: 150,000/mm3 or less
options.quote: HSS assigns a score of 1 for each of seven findings significantly associated with sepsis: Abnormal total leukocyte count, abnormal total PMN count, elevated immature PMN count, elevated immature to total (I:T) PMN ratio, immature to mature (I:M) PMN ratio ≥0.3, platelet count ≤150,000/mm 3 , and pronounced degenerative or toxic changes in PMNs.

scores.name: Therapeutic hypothermia eligibility (NICHD NRN criteria, as endorsed by AAP 2014)
scores.purpose: Screen infants with suspected hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy for whole-body cooling.
scores.quote: Infants offered hypothermia should meet inclusion criteria outlined in published clinical trials (see Table 1).

items.label: Gestational age 36 weeks or more
items.quote: All infants with a gestational age ≥ 36 weeks will be screened for study entry

items.label: Can start cooling (randomise) by 6 hours of age
items.quote: Inability to randomize by 6 hours of age

groups.label: B. Acidosis or perinatal event (either pathway)

items.label: pH 7.0 or less, or base deficit 16 mEq/L or more, on cord or any postnatal sample within 1 hour of age
items.quote: They have a pH ≤ 7.0 or a base deficit ≥ 16m mEq/ L on umbilical cord or any postnatal sample within 1 hour of age.

items.label: pH 7.01 to 7.15, base deficit 10 to 15.9 mEq/L, or no blood gas, AND an acute perinatal event AND either 10-minute Apgar 5 or less or assisted ventilation from birth for at least 10 minutes
items.quote: If, during this interval, they have a pH between 7.01 and 7.15, a base deficit is between 10 and 15.9 mEq/L, or a blood gas is not available, AND they have an acute perinatal event AND either a 10-minute Apgar score ≤ 5 or assisted ventilation initiated at birth and continued for at least 10 minutes.

groups.label: C. Moderate or severe encephalopathy: 1 or more signs in at least 3 of these 6 categories
groups.quote: For this study, encephalopathy is defined as the presence of 1 or more signs in 3 of the following 6 categories:

items.label: Level of consciousness: lethargy, stupor or coma
items.quote: Level of consciousness: lethargy, stupor or coma;

items.label: Tone: hypotonia, flaccid or hypertonia, rigid
items.quote: tone: hypotonia, flaccid or hypertonia, rigid;

items.label: Primitive reflexes: suck weak or absent; Moro incomplete or flaccid
items.quote: Primitive reflexes: a) suck, weak, absent; b) Moro, incomplete, flaccid;

items.label: Autonomic: pupils constricted, unequal, skew deviation or non reactive; bradycardia or variable heart rate; periodic breathing or apnea
items.quote: Autonomic nervous system: a) pupils: constricted, unequal, skew deviation or non reactive to light; b) heart rate: bradycardia, variable heart rate or c) respiration: periodic breathing, apnea.

items.label: Not severely growth restricted (birth weight above 1800 g)
Not moribund (further intensive treatment planned)
items.quote: Infant is moribund and will not receive any further aggressive treatment

notes.text: Seizures also qualify in place of group C in the NICHD trial.
notes.quote: Infants will be candidates for the study when encephalopathy or seizures are present.

notes.text: AAP 2014: cooling within 6 hours of birth for 72 hours for infants above 35 weeks with moderate or severe encephalopathy.
notes.quote: moderate hypothermia initiated within 6 hours of birth and continued for 72 hours is a safe and modestly effective neural rescue strategy for infants born at greater than 35 weeks of gestational age who have clinical evidence of moderate or severe neonatal encephalopathy.

notes.text: AAP 2014 summary of eligibility (worded as a list, logic less explicit than the NICHD record).
notes.quote: Eligibility criteria include a pH of ≤7.0 or a base deficit of ≥16 mmol/L in a sample of umbilical cord blood or blood obtained during the first hour after birth, history of an acute perinatal event, a 10-minute Apgar score of <5, or assisted ventilation initiated at birth and continued for at least 10 minutes.

notes.text: AAP 2014: moderate to severe encephalopathy on neurologic examination is essential; EEG or aEEG abnormality also needed if head cooling is used.
notes.quote: In addition, a neurologic examination demonstrating moderate to severe encephalopathy is essential. If preferential head cooling is used, an abnormal background activity on either EEG or aEEG also is required.

notes.text: AAP 2014: trial parameters.
notes.quote: in all trials infants were at least 35 weeks’ gestation at birth; randomization was completed within 6 hours of birth; the target temperature was 33.5°C to 34.5°C; the intervention period was 72 hours, followed by slow rewarming (0.5°C/hour)

notes.text: AAP 2014: below 35 weeks, mild encephalopathy, longer or deeper cooling only in research.
notes.quote: Cooling infants who are born at less than 35 weeks’ gestation or those who have mild encephalopathy, cooling for longer than 72 hours, cooling at a temperature lower than that used in published clinical trials, and the use of adjuvant therapies should only be performed in a research setting and with informed parental consent.

notes.text: Discrepancies: AAP 2014 says 10-minute Apgar '<5' and base deficit in mmol/L; the NICHD record says '≤ 5' and mEq/L. Gestation: AAP 'greater than 35 weeks', NICHD '≥ 36 weeks'. Groups follow the NICHD record.
Exclusion text in the NICHD record also includes core temperature below 33.5 C for over 1 hour at screening and refusal of consent; not modelled as items.
A newer AAP clinical report (Pediatrics 2026;157(2):e2025073627) exists and was not fetched (publisher blocks automated access). Check whether it supersedes 2014.
